paper.title: Live-Evo: Online Evolution of Agentic Memory from Continuous Feedback
paper.central_claim: Live-Evo, an online self-evolving memory (Experience Bank with feedback-updated weights + Meta-Guideline Bank + verify-before-update write-back) learns from a stream of tasks, improving Brier score 20.8% and market return 12.9% on a 10-week Prophet Arena horizon and transferring to deep-research benchmarks with consistent gains.

provenance.notes: Opus aggregate seat via the configured claude-kimi type fable; no route probing. actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref are null because the subagent runtime exposes no verifiable provider receipt to this worker.

evidence.quote: most existing evolution pipelines are developed for static train/test splits and only approximate online learning by folding static benchmarks, making them brittle under true distribution shift and continuous feedback
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: existing memory evolution is built on static splits and approximates online learning.

evidence.quote: However, none of them focus on evolving on live benchmarks.
evidence.support_explanation: Related-work novelty claim over BoT, ExpeL, AWM, A-Mem, forgetting-based memories.

evidence.quote: by producing and comparing two independent predictions, one guided by the compiled guideline and one as a memory-free baseline, to quantify the contribution of the guideline
evidence.support_explanation: ContrastiveEval: paired memory-on / memory-off run per task as the credit signal.

evidence.quote: when the guideline improves performance, the corresponding experience weights are increased; when it harms performance, the weights are decreased.
evidence.support_explanation: Weight update from the paired gain, applied to all selected experiences.

evidence.quote: Weight_{new}=Weight_{old}+(score_{noexp}-score_{exp})
evidence.support_explanation: Additive, unbounded update from one pair of single stochastic runs (temperature 0.2); no clipping or normalisation is described, and the credit is shared equally by every retrieved experience.

evidence.quote: we not only consider the similarity between experiences and queries, but also multiply it by an experience weight that is updated during the evolution cycle.
evidence.support_explanation: Next-task reading: retrieval score = weight x similarity, so down-weighted entries drop below the similarity threshold.

evidence.quote: if the guideline underperforms, the agent generates a new entry for the Meta-Guideline Bank.
evidence.support_explanation: Meta-guideline (how to compile experience) added on non-positive gain, with no verification step analogous to the experience commit gate.

evidence.quote: We then re-evaluate the task with this candidate experience, and commit it to the experience bank only if it yields a statistically significant improvement over the original memory-on score.
evidence.support_explanation: Verify-before-update gate. The candidate is built from the stored trajectory of the same task and re-evaluated on that same task, so a candidate that encodes the answer can pass; no significance test is specified beyond a min_brier_improvement threshold.

evidence.quote: We enforce strict time-based retrieval on google-search tool to prevent information leakage past the close time.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors' leakage guard for the live-prediction benchmark (500 tasks over the latest 10 weeks).

evidence.quote: We use serper api as the google-search api and apply the time filter by editing the queries.
evidence.support_explanation: The time guard is implemented by editing the query, not by verifying result publication dates.

evidence.locator: Appendix A.2 Table 5 (showcase task, Oct 16 2025 NFL game)
evidence.quote: Identified close 33-31 victory conditions.
evidence.support_explanation: The memory-on agent's reasoning cites the final score of a game it is supposed to forecast before kick-off: post-close information leaked through search despite the guard.

evidence.quote: Results confirm the game conclusion
evidence.support_explanation: Search observation in the showcase trajectory states the game outcome, corroborating that the time filter is leaky; the memory-off baseline shares the tool, so the leak may affect both arms differently.

evidence.quote: All experiments use a temperature =0.2, with bad_case_percentile =0.3, min_brier_improvement =0.05, and experience _similarity_threshold =0.5.
evidence.support_explanation: Hyperparameters stated (single configuration, tuning protocol absent); appendix gives a minimum weighted similarity of 0.3, inconsistent with 0.5 here.

evidence.quote: a future-prediction benchmark spanning the latest 10 weeks with 500 tasks in total
evidence.support_explanation: Evaluation size: about 50 tasks per week, processed sequentially.
Weekly Brier W1-W10 and average for the full system.
Memory-off control with the same search agent; W1 is worse for Live-Evo (0.19 vs 0.18), W9 ties and W10 differs by 0.01.
Only memory baseline; ReMem beats Live-Evo in W3 and W4/W10 are within 0.01; implementation and budget parity unspecified.

evidence.quote: Live-Evo consistently outperforms the base agent across all weeks.
evidence.support_explanation: Contradicted by Table 1 W1 (0.19 vs 0.18) and W9 (equal 0.13).

evidence.quote: Notably, the performance gap between the two agents widens over time, indicating that
evidence.support_explanation: Table 1 gaps are largest in W5-W6 (0.10, 0.07) and shrink to 0.00/0.01 in W9-W10, so 'widens over time' is not clear from the table (Fig 3a values not readable).
Headline numbers; reported relative improvements (20.8%, 12.9%) do not follow from the shown values (0.19 to 0.14 is -26%; 1.24 to 1.46 is +17.7%), so the aggregation is unclear.
Gains shrink sharply on other backbones (GPT-4.1 3.0%/4.4%, GPT-5-mini 4.5%/1.6%, Qwen3-8B 3.5%/0.5%); the headline is the GPT-4.1-mini configuration.

evidence.quote: Qwen-DeepResearch 0.43 MiroFlow 0.45 ReMem 0.40 Live-Evo (ours) 0.46
evidence.support_explanation: Transfer table has no memory-off Live-Evo/base row, so the memory contribution is not isolated; margin over MiroFlow is 0.01 and no variance is given.

evidence.quote: We split the benchmark into 10 folds, learn experience sequentially across folds, and report the overall average accuracy.
evidence.support_explanation: Xbench is a static benchmark folded into pseudo-streams, the very practice the paper criticises in prior work (E001).

evidence.quote: w/o weight-update 0.17 +17.01% 1.34 -8.01% w/o meta-guideline 0.16 +10.88% 1.41 -3.42% w/o guideline-compile 0.16 +11.56% 1.16 -20.40% w/o active-retrieve 0.17 +14.97% 1.22 -16.77%

evidence.quote: Removing any single module consistently degrades performance in both Brier Score and market return, indicating that each component is non-trivial
evidence.support_explanation: Author reading of Table 4; the w/o meta-guideline change in return (-3.42%) is small.

evidence.quote: its reliance on the dense environment feedback ensures robust calibration but may limit applicability in settings with sparse or subjective feedback
evidence.support_explanation: Stated boundary: dense feedback is required.

evidence.quote: Such mismatches lead to consistently poor downstream performance and are therefore downweighted over time.
evidence.support_explanation: Anecdotal evidence that a hallucinated experience was down-weighted; only two entries shown.

evidence.quote: Over-generalization of domain-specific lessons across fundamentally different task types and contexts.
evidence.support_explanation: Shows a generated meta-guideline entry (applicability check) produced from a failure.

evidence.quote: Concretely, we execute the agent again without the compiled guideline.
evidence.support_explanation: Credit signal requires a second full agent run for every task; cost is not quantified anywhere and baselines are not given the equivalent budget.

evidence.quote: Live-Evo, the first online-evolving agentic memory system specifically designed for benchmarks with continuous, real-world feedback
evidence.support_explanation: Priority claim; closest online-memory baseline ReMem is only compared empirically, and AWM/ExpeL/A-Mem are named only in text.

evidence.quote: Incorporate dynamic, up-to-date info (roster, coaching) as the event approaches.
evidence.support_explanation: The retrieved experience pushes the memory-on arm toward searches close to the event, which is where a query-edit time filter is most likely to leak results. Leakage can therefore differ between the memory-on and memory-off arms; it is not a neutral common-mode error.

evidence.quote: For each new task batch, the agent operates through four stages:
evidence.support_explanation: Weights are updated inside the per-task loop of a batch, but the paper never states when each task's outcome becomes available relative to the close times of later tasks in the same batch. That information-timing condition is central to a live-forecasting memory, and it is unspecified.

evidence.quote: Brier Score: 0.5329
evidence.support_explanation: For truth Cincinnati=1, the baseline's (0.35, 0.65) gives multiclass Brier 0.845 by Eq. 1, and Live-Evo's (0.55, 0.45) gives 0.405; the table prints 0.5329 and 0.2500. The showcase metric does not follow the stated formula.

gap.author_gap: Memory-evolution pipelines assume static train/test splits and approximate online learning by folding; under true streaming and shift, stored experience becomes stale or misleading and must be actively curated.
gap.checked_gap: Plausible and specific (staleness under drift, when and how to use experience), but the paper does not measure drift or staleness directly; evidence is the aggregate gain, a two-entry weight case study and an ablation of weights.
gap.lineage_closest_adjacent: Ancestors in local text: ExpeL, BoT, Agent Workflow Memory, A-Mem, forgetting memories (MemoryBank), ReMem (Wei et al. 2025b) as the online-fold baseline. Only ReMem is compared experimentally; the paper's own priority claim is 'first'.
gap.residue: Online memory still lacks a statistically sound commit (same-task test), a size bound/retirement, and noise-robust credit across co-retrieved entries.
gap.stakes: Live forecasting where stale experience degrades calibration and market returns.
gap.method_response: Per-task paired counterfactual credits weights; meta-guidelines make the compile step learnable; gated write-back controls growth.
gap.remaining_gap: Whether the weight decay handles drift beyond 10 weeks and whether gains survive leak-free retrieval remain open.
unresolved: Direct evidence of distribution shift or stale-experience harm
Closest neighbours' original texts (ReMem, ExpeL) are not in the package; difference rests on authors' description

claims.text: Live-Evo improves Brier by 20.8% and market return by 12.9% on a 10-week Prophet Arena stream over a memory-free agent.
claims.setting: 500 resolved tasks processed weekly, GPT-4.1-mini, serper search with query-edit time filter
claims.baseline_control: Live-Evo w/o Experience (same agent), Base Model, MiroFlow, Qwen Deep Research, ReMem
claims.selection_vs_test: Memory evolves on the reported stream; later weeks evaluated with earlier-week memory; no frozen-bank or independent stream; hyperparameter tuning protocol not described
claims.result_denominator: Avg Brier 0.14 vs 0.19 (w/o Experience) vs 0.16 (ReMem); weeks where Live-Evo is not better: W1, W9 (tie); single run
claims.allowed_conclusion: On this stream, Live-Evo's Brier is lower on average than a memory-free agent and ReMem; absolute and relative gains are uncertain because of search leakage evidence, single-run variance and unclear percentage arithmetic.

claims.text: Each component (weight update, meta-guideline, compile, active retrieval) is essential.
claims.result_denominator: Brier +10.9% to +17.0% worse, return -3.4% to -20.4%; single run
claims.allowed_conclusion: Removing any of four components worsens both metrics in a single run; gate and meta-guideline verification untested; meta-guideline effect on return is small.

claims.text: Experience weights down-weight misleading entries and keep helpful ones.
claims.setting: Case study of lowest/highest weight entries
claims.allowed_conclusion: Illustrative anecdote; no systematic precision of weight ranking against entry harm.

claims.text: Gains transfer across backbones and to deep research benchmarks.
claims.baseline_control: w/o Mem per backbone; no memory-off row for Xbench
claims.result_denominator: Brier gains 3.0-20.8%, return gains 0.5-12.9%; Xbench 0.46 vs 0.45/0.43/0.40
claims.allowed_conclusion: Directionally positive on four backbones in Prophet Arena; the Xbench claim of consistent gains is unsupported without a memory-off control and variance.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: On the reported 10-week stream, the memory system had lower average Brier than the same agent without experience and than ReMem, and each of four ablated components moved both metrics the same way (single run). Whether the gain survives leak-free retrieval is not established: the paper's own showcase shows post-close information reaching the memory-on arm.
unresolved: Effect of the commit gate and of meta-guidelines as an improver
assessment.level_reason: Both seats retained; re-checked. Weights, experiences and meta-guidelines written from earlier weeks are read on later, different tasks, and the same agent without experience is the store-off control. Scoped: the evidence is author-reported and single-run, and temporal isolation of web search is contradicted by the showcase (E.holdout 0), so the magnitude of the retained gain is uncertain. Not improver.

G.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. Staleness and how-to-use-experience under live streams are specific gaps. Neighbours (ExpeL, BoT, AWM, A-Mem, ReMem) are named and ReMem is run. Not 4: staleness is never measured, and the 'first' claim is asserted against one empirical neighbour.

M.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. Paired on/off credit, weight × similarity retrieval, a learnable compile instruction bank and gated write-back are a coherent, reconstructable response. Not 4: the credit is uniform over co-retrieved entries and rests on one noisy paired difference.

X.reason: Opus sides with sol. Retrieval and weight formulas and the main parameters are given. But a key condition of a live loop, when each outcome becomes visible to later tasks in the same batch, is unspecified (opus:O02). The commit gate is described both as 'statistically significant' and as a 0.05 single-task threshold on the generating task. Meta-guidelines are added without any gate, there is no rollback or size bound, and the similarity thresholds conflict (0.5 vs 0.3) → anchor 2.

E.measurement.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. Brier and market return fit the task. The reported numbers have arithmetic problems: the headline percentages do not follow from Table 2, and Table 5 Brier values do not follow Eq. 1 (opus:O03). Per A2, the search leakage is charged to E.holdout and is not counted here; son55's reason double-counted it.

E.causality.reason: Opus sides with son55. The same agent without experience, ReMem, a four-component ablation (weights, meta-guidelines, compile, active retrieval) and four backbones all point the same way. The extra memory-off run is a learning-time cost of the credit signal, not extra prediction-time budget for the reported arm, so it is charged to E.cost. Not 4: the commit gate is unablated, there is no memory-off row on Xbench, ReMem parity is unspecified, and every comparison is a single run.

E.holdout.reason: Opus sides with sol. For a live-forecasting claim the holdout question is temporal isolation. The paper asserts 'strict time-based retrieval' (sol:E005), implements it by editing queries (sol:E007), and its own showcase trajectory reads 'Results confirm the game conclusion' and reasons from the final 33-31 score (sol:E008, son55:E011). The retrieved experience steers the credited arm toward near-event searches (opus:O01). No audit bounds how many tasks are affected. The forward-in-time ordering of weeks is a real design strength, but it cannot certify a prospective evaluation when outcomes can be retrieved from the web. Anchor 0: the evidence contradicts the isolation claim. It is not not_reported: the evidence exists and refutes the claim.

E.statistics.reason: Both seats 1; re-checked (A2 ladder). Sample size (500) and weekly rows (including weeks lost or tied) are given; there are no seeds, intervals or tests on 0.01–0.05 Brier margins.

E.cost.reason: Opus sides with sol (precedent r09b AgentDevel: qualitative cost information only → not_reported). The method states that every task is run twice and that candidates are re-evaluated (son55:E029), and caps turns at 20 (sol:E011). No tokens, dollars, calls or time are reported for any arm, and the baselines get no matched budget.

resolutions.reason: controlled_diagnostic_design not retained. The paired run is a credit signal inside the improvement loop, not an evaluation instrument built to measure a property; H29's S1 counterfactual already describes it.

All three are real correspondences. H29: entry weights are updated from with/without-memory gains. H30: commit only after a re-evaluation improvement, with soft retirement via down-weighting (medium fit: no size bound or hard retirement). H00: failure-reason/improvement entries are summarised from poorly solved trajectories. sol's note that the gate is not full H30 governance is reflected in the medium fit.
